learning_objective: 🎯 Cross the borders! Understand the complexities, documents, and institutions involved in buying and selling goods across different nations.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: International business involves transactions across national boundaries. It faces complexities like dealing with different currencies, varying legal systems, distance, and high transportation risks compared to domestic trade.

An exporter receives an inquiry, gets the order, obtains a Letter of Credit (payment guarantee) from the importer's bank, manufactures/procures goods, clears customs, and ships the goods along with a Bill of Lading.

1. Proforma Invoice: A quotation sent by the exporter. 2. Letter of Credit: A bank's guarantee that the importer will pay. 3. Bill of Lading: A receipt from the shipping company that goods are loaded on the ship.
An international organization formed in 1995 (replacing GATT) to promote free and fair trade between nations by reducing tariffs and settling trade disputes.

fun_activity.title: 📜 The Trust Issue
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine selling 1,000 laptops to a stranger in Germany. You fear he won't pay. He fears you won't ship. Solution? The 'Letter of Credit'! His bank promises your bank the money *only* after you prove you shipped the laptops. Problem solved!

exam_tips: 📌 The 'Letter of Credit' is the most crucial document in international trade to ensure payment security. Know its definition.
📌 Distinguish between 'Mate's Receipt' (given by the captain of the ship when goods are loaded) and 'Bill of Lading' (the official contract and receipt from the shipping company).
📌 Why go international? Firms do it to earn foreign exchange, utilize excess production capacity, and improve business vision.
quick_recap: ⭐ International business includes not just export/import of goods, but also services, licensing, franchising, and foreign investments.
⭐ The IEC (Import Export Code) number is a mandatory registration required to start international trade in India.
⭐ Certificate of Origin is a document required by customs to verify the country where the goods were manufactured.
